> **How glass is recycled — and why it often isn’t**
> 
> The technical process is simple. Collected glass is sorted by colour, either by hand or increasingly by optical scanners. It is then washed to remove labels and residue, crushed into small fragments known as cullet, and melted in a furnace at around 1,500 degrees. The molten glass is moulded into new containers, cooled slowly to prevent cracking, and inspected before distribution. Glass can pass through this cycle indefinitely without loss of quality, which distinguishes it from plastic and paper.
> 
> In practice, much collected glass never completes the cycle. The main obstacle is colour. Cullet must be sorted precisely: a small quantity of green glass in a clear batch ruins the whole load. Where collection systems mix colours — as most kerbside schemes do — separation becomes expensive and the material is often used instead as road aggregate, a low-value application that is still counted as recycling in official figures.
> 
> Weight is the second obstacle. Glass is heavy, so transporting it to a furnace can consume more energy than the recycling saves if the distance is large. In countries with few furnaces, the environmental case for collecting glass at all becomes surprisingly weak.

writing.de_tom_tat: Task 1, ≥150 từ: mô tả quy trình tái chế giấy gồm 6 giai đoạn.
writing.bai_mau:
The diagram illustrates the process by which used paper is recycled into new paper products. Overall, the procedure consists of six main stages, beginning with collection and ending with the production of finished paper.

At the first stage, waste paper is collected from households and offices and transported to a recycling facility. Once it arrives, the material is sorted by hand and by machine, so that unsuitable items such as plastic and metal can be removed.

The sorted paper is then shredded into small pieces and mixed with water and chemicals to form a pulp. In the fourth stage, this pulp passes through a de-inking process, in which air bubbles and detergent are used to lift printing ink away from the fibres. The pulp emerging from this stage is noticeably paler.

Subsequently, the cleaned pulp is pressed between heavy rollers, which remove most of the remaining water and flatten the material into thin sheets. Finally, the sheets are dried, cut to size and rolled, after which the finished paper is ready for distribution.

The cycle can then begin again, as the recycled paper eventually returns to the collection stage.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Nêu đủ 6 giai đoạn theo đúng thứ tự, có Overview nói rõ số giai đoạn và điểm bắt đầu/kết thúc. Câu cuối chỉ ra tính chu trình — chi tiết quan trọng mà nhiều thí sinh bỏ qua.
Từ nối trình tự đa dạng: At the first stage · Once it arrives · then · In the fourth stage · Subsequently · Finally · after which. Không lặp "then" liên tục.
recycling facility · sorted by hand and by machine · shredded · pulp · de-inking process · detergent · fibres · pressed between rollers · cut to size · distribution.

Bị động xuyên suốt (is collected, is sorted, are used, are dried) — đúng chuẩn tả quy trình · mệnh đề quan hệ (in which air bubbles are used, which remove most of the water) · mệnh đề rút gọn (beginning with collection, emerging from this stage).

dang_hoc: Tả quy trình thì bị động là mặc định, vì người thực hiện không quan trọng: is collected, is sorted, are dried.
Dùng hiện tại đơn cho quy trình (không phải quá khứ), vì nó luôn diễn ra như vậy.
Bộ từ nối trình tự cần thuộc: At the first stage · Once… · Subsequently · After that · Finally · after which.
Nếu quy trình là chu trình thì phải nói rõ ở câu cuối — đây là điểm nhiều người bỏ mất.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Dùng chủ động với "they" chung chung ("they collect the paper") → nên dùng bị động.
❌ Lặp "then… then… then" cả bài → mất điểm Cohesion.
❌ Đếm sai số giai đoạn trong Overview → kiểm tra lại trước khi nộp.
❌ Thêm ý kiến ("this is good for the environment") → Task 1 chỉ mô tả.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 1 — Transport: How do you travel to work? / Is public transport good? / Would you cycle more?

cau_tra_loi.hoi: How do you travel to work?
cau_tra_loi.mau: By motorbike, like most people here. It takes about twenty-five minutes, though considerably longer if I leave during rush hour.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Có số liệu thời gian và điều kiện ngoại lệ — chi tiết cụ thể.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Is public transport good where you live?
cau_tra_loi.mau: It's improving. The first metro line opened recently and it's made a real difference on that route, but coverage is still limited and buses can be slow.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Cân bằng: nêu tiến bộ rồi nêu hạn chế còn lại.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Would you cycle more if there were better facilities?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Definitely. The main deterrent is safety — there simply aren't dedicated lanes. If proper cycle routes existed, I'd use them most days.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Câu điều kiện loại 2 đúng ngữ cảnh giả định. "deterrent" là từ vựng band cao.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Trả lời có số liệu, có điều kiện.
rush hour · coverage · deterrent · dedicated lanes.
If proper cycle routes existed, I'd use them (điều kiện loại 2).

meo_noi: Câu hỏi giả định ("Would you… if…") thì phải trả lời bằng điều kiện loại 2.
"deterrent", "coverage", "facilities" — từ vựng chủ đề giao thông đáng thuộc.
